# Sudoers text verification

The source boundary is a slice of characters from the stable parser, not a call to an installed `sudo`. Opening a trusted file, decoding its bytes, resolving OS identities and executing commands are separate boundaries. [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) gives the target statements and records where a proposed property is too strong.

| Question | Evidence |
|---|---|
| What does a file mean, including errors? | [Executable reference parser](../spec/SudoersSpec/Syntax/README.md), [exact clean-file grammar and uniqueness](../spec/SudoersSpec/Grammar/SudoUnique.lean), [recovery and source accounting](../spec/SudoersSpec/Syntax/Recovery.lean). Diagnostic spans locate errors; they need not cover all skipped characters. |
| Which parser does Lean check? | [`parse_sudoers_refines`](../lean/SudoRsProofs/Parser/Directives/Main.lean) connects the extracted stable Rust entry point to the reference on an entire character slice, including the order of accepted items and errors. [`ordinaryPolicy_roundTrip`](../differential/Differential/OrdinaryPolicyRange.lean) covers the permission rules printed by the ordinary generator, for every seed under its stated snapshot. |
| How are lines turned into policy? | [Collection and scoping spec](../spec/SudoersSpec/Analysis/Collect.lean), [analyzed text](../lean/SudoRsProofs/Parser/Analysis/Text.lean), [include traversal](../lean/SudoRsProofs/Parser/Analysis/Includes.lean). The latter uses a finite snapshot of the actual include calls; it does not verify a filesystem. |
| Does a real check use those rules and Defaults? | [`text_to_authorization` and `TextAgreement.clean_unique`](../lean/SudoRsProofs/Parser/EndToEnd.lean) cover include-free text, including recovered syntax errors. They compare the extracted `analyze_text`, `Sudoers::check` and `Judgement::authorization` to the reference; native environment sets are compared by membership. [No accepted Defaults](../lean/SudoRsProofs/Parser/NoDefaults.lean) leaves the initial settings in force. |
| What is assumed or only tested? | [Trusted models, size bounds and external oracles](../lean/ASSUMPTIONS.md#parser-and-analysis-boundaries), [Lean vs Rust tests and observer versions](P0.md), [separate C sudo comparison](C-SUDO.md#larger-corpus-limits-of-the-classification). Test counts apply only to the specified corpus, host, observer and revision. |

From the repository root, `nix develop -c proofs/check.sh tokens spec lean axioms rust` checks the proof projects and the sudoers unit tests. `nix develop -c proofs/check.sh extract` independently checks generated-source drift. Neither gate compares sudo-rs with C sudo or exercises the installation and privilege boundary.
